subject: TTFT & streaming requirements — follow-up (FinLytics)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: TTFT & streaming requirements — follow-up (FinLytics)

Hi Samir — great to speak today, thanks for the time. Quick recap from our discovery and the key items we agreed to validate in a TTFT/streaming pilot: 

Summary (high level):
- Primary goal: streaming responses for live analyst UI with target Time-to-first-token (TTFT) and chunk cadence guarantees.
- Target p95 TTFT: 150 ms (we noted your team may accept p95 <= 200 ms; please confirm).
- p99 TTFT target: aiming for <= 350 ms for peak-critical flows.
- Streaming: web clients prefer SSE, mobile clients prefer WebSocket. Need chunk cadence of ~200-300 ms (max 350 ms) for smooth token-by-token UI updates.
- Throughput & concurrency: baseline expected steady-state 200 RPS, typical concurrency ~500 concurrent live sessions, burst to 1000 RPS for market open spikes.
- Model & perf note: we discussed using a quantized 16/4-bit variant for cost and latency tradeoffs; we'll recommend model variants after we see sample payloads.

Ask / next steps:
1) Can you confirm the p95/p99 TTFT targets (150/350 ms vs the 200/350 cushions)?
2) Please share a small set of representative prompt payloads (sample messages, avg/95th prompt sizes) and expected tokenization — I've attached a sample template.
3) Tell us if SSE-only is required for web, or if WebSocket is acceptable. Also call out any firewall/proxy constraints.
4) We'll spin up a short TTFT pilot on Redwood (no production data retained beyond audit period) and run synthetic traffic that mirrors your concurrency pattern. Dev will coordinate the pilot setup and telemetry access.

I attached a one-page requirements sheet (FinLytics_TTFT_requirements.xlsx) and created a short shared doc with our plan: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBcD2eXAMPLE-ttft-requirements

If that all sounds good, can we schedule a 30-min pilot kickoff next week? Available windows: Tue/Wed 10–12 PT.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | (415) 555-0126

--
Attachment: FinLytics_TTFT_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)

From: Samir Shah <samir@finlytics.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia@finlytics.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming requirements — follow-up (FinLytics)

Thanks Aditya — good recap. A few clarifications from our side after chatting with the infra team: 

- TTFT targets: we can commit to p95 <= 200 ms for the majority of flows; for critical workflows (real-time market alerts) we need p95 <= 150 ms if possible but can accept up to 200 ms initially. p99 should be <= 350 ms.
- Chunk cadence: target average 200–300 ms between chunks; maximum acceptable gap 350 ms. We prefer SSE for web clients because of current proxy setups, but we are open to WebSocket for mobile apps.
- Throughput: planned steady-state ~150–250 RPS. Peak bursts (market open) can hit ~900–1,000 RPS for short windows. Concurrent live sessions estimated ~400–600.
- Security/residency: data stays in US, and we need SOC2 + basic audit logs for the pilot.

I've attached a small archive of sample payloads (sample_payloads.json) and a short CSV with median/95th prompt sizes. We can do Tue 10:30 PT next week for kickoff — that works for Olivia and me.

Appreciate you setting this up.

—Samir
Samir Shah
Head of Platform Engineering, FinLytics
samir@finlytics.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

--
Attachment: sample_payloads.json (JSON, ~3KB)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -0700

Thanks Samir — that all makes sense and aligns with what we discussed. Quick replies to the points: 

- We'll treat p95=200 ms as the short-term acceptability target and prioritize p95=150 ms for the critical alert flows during the pilot. p99 <= 350 ms is noted.
- SSE for web + WebSocket for mobile is fine — Dev will validate proxy behavior during the kickoff.
- Pilot plan: Dev will provision a dedicated test environment in our US region, run a set of synthetic and replayed payloads (using your sample_payloads.json), and capture TTFT, chunk cadence, p95/p99 latencies, and end-to-end client-side timings.

Dev — can you schedule the pilot for Tue 10:30 PT and confirm what artifacts you need from FinLytics (e.g., keys, sample payloads, expected request concurrency profile)? Also please confirm the telemetry we'll deliver (p50/p90/p95/p99 TTFT, chunk cadence histogram, request/second heatmap, logs retention window).

Samir/Olivia — we will only request minimal telemetry access and will not persist raw user content beyond the pilot retention window; we'll provide SOC2 evidence and an audit log package as part of the onboarding checklist.

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

Aditya Rao

Hi all — I'll take point on the pilot. Confirming the Tue 10:30 PT kickoff (calendar invite to follow).

What we need from FinLytics before kickoff:
- Sample payloads (you already sent sample_payloads.json — thanks). If you have a short list of 10 representative prompts (median and 95th), please drop that into the shared doc.
- Expected concurrency profile (RPS over a 5/15/60-min window) — a simple CSV is fine.
- Any proxy/agent IP allowlist entries for the sandbox if you have strict egress rules.

What we'll produce during/after the pilot:
- Telemetry: p50/p90/p95/p99 TTFT (server-side), chunk cadence histogram (client-observed), end-to-end latency distribution, RPS heatmap, and a short summary with improvement suggestions (batching, kv-cache, model variant).
- Artifacts: test run logs (redacted), a short video capture of streaming behavior in the sample web UI, and the audit package for SOC2 checklist.

I'll provision the environment in the US region and create a temporary telemetry dashboard and a secure upload link for any additional payloads: https://files.redwood.com/upload/finlytics-pilot-2026 (link expires in 7 days).

If you can confirm the concurrency CSV and drop any final prompt examples into the doc before Tue 08:00 PT, we'll be ready to execute.

Thanks —
